arabic text:
SAKINA UTHO. MERI JAAN UTHO. REHAEE MILI. CHALO
GAR CHALE
YE KARTI THI MAA, LAHAD PE BUKAA. MERI LADLI,
CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
Sakina, rise—my beloved, rise. We have been
freed; come, let us go home. Her
mother lamented beside the grave: ‘My
darling, come, let us go home.’

arabic text:
YAHA SE CHALO, CHALE KARBALA. WAHI SE TUMHE,
MILENGE CHACHA. SITAM JO HUWE, BATAANA UNE.
DIKHAANA UNHE, YE KURTA JALAA. CHACHA JAAN KO,
DIKHANA ZARA, RIDAA KHUN BHARE, CHALO GAR
CHALE.
english translation text:
Come, let us leave here and go to
Karbala. There you will meet your uncle. Tell
him of every cruelty you endured. Show him
this burnt dress, and show your dear uncle
the bloodstained veil. Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
BATAANA UNHE, KABHI SAKTIYA. MILI JIS KADAR, TUJE
GURKHIYA. HAMARI RIDAA, LUTI KIS TARHA. CHINI JIS
TARHA, TERI BALIYA. BATAANA UNE, BUJI KIS TARHA,
TERI TISHNAGI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
Tell him how many hardships and rebukes you
suffered; how our veils were looted and your
earrings torn away. Tell him how your thirst
was finally quenched. Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
PADAR SE MILO, TO DIL JOEE HO. BATAANA UNHE,
BAHOT ROI HO. KASAM LO AGAR, TUMHARE BINA.
SAKINA KABHI, KAHI SOYI HO. LAHAD BAP KI, MILE JAB
TUJE, TO KEHNA YAHI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
When you meet your father, let him console your heart.
Tell him how much you wept. Ask him whether Sakina
ever slept anywhere without him. When you reach your father’s
grave, say only this: come, let us go home.

arabic text:
LAHAD JAB MILE, TUJE BHAI KI. TO KEHNA USE, MERI
LADLI. REHAEE MILI, HAME KAID SE. HAME AB NAHI,
AZIYAT KOI. MERE BE ZUBA, UTHO GAR CHALE, SHABI
HAI NABI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
When you reach your brother’s grave, tell him, ‘My darling,
we have been freed from prison; no suffering remains for
us now.’ My speechless child, rise and come home,
O image of the Prophet—come, let us go home.

arabic text:
LABE AL KAMA, TU KARNA FUGAA. TERI MOJ HAI, ABHI
TAKH RAWA. MERI PYAS PAR, HUYE JO FIDA. CHACHA
KE MERE, HAI BAZU KAHAA. KAHAA MASHK HAI, KAHAA
HAI ALAM, KAHAA HAI ZARI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
At the bank of the Alqama, raise your lament; its waves
are still flowing. Ask: ‘Where are the arms of my uncle
who sacrificed himself for my thirst? Where are the water-skin,
the standard and the shrine?’ Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
NA AB GHAM KOI, NA UFTAD HAI. WO ZANJIR SE, AB
AAZAD HAI. PUPHI BHI TERI, TERE SATH HAI. TERE
SATH HI, WO SAJJAD HAI. MERI GHAM ZADAA, SHABE
GHAM KATI, SAHAR HO CHUKI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
There is no grief or calamity now; he is free from
his chains. Your aunt is with you, and Sajjad is with
you too. My grief-stricken child, the night of sorrow has
passed and dawn has come. Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
LABO PAR TERE, YAHI BAAT THI. WATAN JAYENGE,
KABHI HAM PUPHI. TUJE SHIMR KA, NAHI KHOF AB.
SATAYENGE NA, TUJE AB SHAKI. NIKAL KAYD SE, SHURU
HAM KARE, NAYI ZINDAGI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
These words were always upon your lips: ‘Aunt, will we ever
return home?’ You need no longer fear Shimr, nor will
the cruel ones torment you. Let us leave this prison
and begin a new life. Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
GHARIBO KA YE, LUTA KAFELA. WIDA HO KE PHIR,
WATAN JAYENGE. TUJE PAYENGI, JO SUGHRA TERI. TO
BIMAR KO, MILENGI DAWA. GALE MIL KE PHIR, BOHOT
ROYENGI, WO BEHNA TERI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
This plundered caravan of the forsaken will bid farewell and
return home. When your sister Sughra sees you, the
ailing girl will find her cure. She will embrace
you and weep greatly. Come, let us go home.

arabic text:
MAZAR-E NABI, LARAZ JAYENGA. BAHEN JAB TERI,
KARENGI BUKAA. KAHA HAI CHACHA, KAHA HAI PADAR.
KAHA HAI BATAA, BHARA GAR MERA. SUNA NE USE, YE
RUDAAD-E GHAM, YEHI BEBASI, CHALO GAR CHALE.
english translation text:
The Prophet’s shrine will tremble when your sister begins to
lament: ‘Where is my uncle? Where is my father? Tell
me—where is my once-full home?’ We must tell her this
tale of grief and helplessness. Come, let us go home.

arabic text: (SAKINA UTHO. MERI JAAN UTHO. REHAEE MILI. CHALO\nGAR CHALE)
english translation text: Sakina, rise—my beloved, rise. We have been\nfreed; come, let us go home.
